newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issuance shifts into high gear.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issuance shifts into high gear.

text.p: Corporate bond primary market activity has shifted into high gear as issuers rush to finance debt amid lower U.S. Treasury yields, dealers said.
"There's no official calendar yet; however, we've heard a number of names circulating the market," said one syndicate source.
Dealers said Friday's U.S. Treasury rally, which sent the yield on the T-bond below 7.00 percent, has lured issuers off the sidelines and into the new issue arena as yields remain lower.

Issuers who were recently kept at bay by higher Treasury yields and fears of a potential Federal Reserve hike in interest rates are expected to take full advantage of the favorable rate environment and meet their financing needs now, dealers added.
"We should see a lot of activity this week with yields at these new levels," said another syndicate source.
Meanwhile, on Monday, Bank of Boston priced $200 million in A3/BBB-plus rated 10-year subordinated notes to yield 65 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.
Another $1.350 billion in a three-part debt offering is expected to come to market out of Nationsbank, syndicate sources said.
The deal is expected to consist of $500 milion five-year debt, $500 million 10-year debt and $350 million of a 20-year issue, they added.
In addition, another $1.0 billion is expected to price out of Ford Motor Credit Corp via a global debt offering, syndicate sources said.
Daimler Benz is also expected to price $500 million in 10-year debt via JP Morgan Securities, sources added.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was trading off 2/32 at 97-12/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
